title: What do we call a number just above ten thousand?
description: Tanvi lays ten thousand tokens with a few small tokens beside them in her classroom in Pune. The video writes each number and says its name.
teaching_notes: One idea: a zero is not read aloud, only the places with tokens are said. Watch for the child who says the zero places.

source: One 10,000 token with two 1 tokens, one 10,000 token with on
video_script.why: The child can write ten thousand but has not yet named numbers just above it.
video_script.substitution: Add the small tokens to ten thousand, write the digits in the chart, and say only the places that hold tokens.
video_script.anchor: Tanvi's token tray in her classroom in Pune
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says ten thousand one ten for one ten thousand token and one ten token. A zero is not read aloud and the ten token is only ten.
video_script.payoff_line: a zero is not said aloud

final_answer.value: 10,002 is ten thousand two, 10,010 is ten thousand ten and 10,024 is ten thousand twenty-four
final_answer.spoken: ten thousand two, ten thousand ten and ten thousand twenty four

never_show: the your-turn answer 10,053 and ten thousand fifty three
maths_rules: token values: a 10,000 token is worth 10,000; a 10 token is worth 10; a 1 token is worth 1
one 10,000 token and two 1 tokens: 10,000 + 2 = 10,002, ten thousand two
one 10,000 token and one 10 token: 10,000 + 10 = 10,010, ten thousand ten
one 10,000 token, two 10 tokens and four 1 tokens: 10,000 + 20 + 4 = 10,024, ten thousand twenty four
the chart for each number has TTh 1, then Th 0, H 0 and a zero or digit in T and O
slip: reading ten thousand one ten for 10,010
your turn: one 10,000 token, five 10 tokens and three 1 tokens; 10,000 + 50 + 3 = 10,053; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: add the small tokens to 10,000, then say only the places that hold tokens. Wrong idea: saying the zero places aloud. The token tray stays as the anchor; the chart builds on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='trays'/>Tanvi sets out three trays in her classroom in Pune. Each tray has one ten thousand token.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Tray one has two one tokens. Tray two has one ten token. Tray three has two ten tokens and four one tokens.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each number and say its name.

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>A ten thousand token is worth ten thousand, whatever tray it sits on.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>A ten token is worth ten, and a one token is worth one.
<bookmark mark='chart'/>A column with no token in it holds a zero, so the other digits stay in place.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>One big token and one ten token. I say ten thousand one ten.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The empty columns hold zeros, and a zero is not said aloud.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Only the places that hold tokens are said when we read the number.

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Tray one is ten thousand with two ones added on.
<bookmark mark='name'/>We say the big part first, and then the ones that come after it. That is ten thousand two.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Tray two is ten thousand with one ten added on. We say the big part, then ten, which is ten thousand ten.
